evals.name: snapshot-happy-path-nfs
evals.prompt: Take a crash-consistent snapshot of the Oracle SID orcl on host i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 in us-east-1. Retention label 'nightly'. It's NFS-mounted on FSx for ONTAP.
expectations: Resolves mapped ONTAP volumes for DATA_FILES/CONTROL_FILES/REDO_LOGS/ARCHIVE_LOGS before any mutation
Does not call aws ssm send-command from the operator machine
Runs topology discovery and confirms deploymentType=standalone before any mutation
Presents a confirmation naming the retention label and effect before creating the consistency group/snapshot
Uses consistency_type=crash and never attempts RMAN BEGIN BACKUP/END BACKUP
Waits for an explicit affirmative before the mutating ONTAP calls
Validates the result with validate_operation_result.sh ... snapshot
Reports the consistency group UUID, group snapshot UUID, and member snapshots for all 4 file types

evals.name: snapshot-rac-source-refused
evals.prompt: Snapshot Oracle SID prod1 on host i-0bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb, us-east-1, retention 'rac-test'. (Topology discovery reports cluster_database=TRUE.)
expectations: Runs topology discovery before attempting any snapshot
Refuses to proceed once RAC (cluster_database=TRUE) is detected
States that only single-instance (non-RAC) Oracle is supported

evals.name: snapshot-dataguard-standby-refused
evals.prompt: Take a snapshot of Oracle SID stdby1 on host i-0ccccccccccccccc, us-west-2, retention 'dg-test'. (Topology discovery reports database_role=PHYSICAL STANDBY.)
expectations: Runs topology discovery before attempting any snapshot
Refuses to proceed once database_role is not PRIMARY
States that Data Guard standby instances are not supported

evals.name: snapshot-dataguard-primary-allowed
evals.prompt: Take a snapshot of Oracle SID prod1 on host i-0ccccccccccccccc, us-west-2, retention 'dg-test'. (Topology discovery reports database_role=PRIMARY with one standby destination and log_archive_config set.)
expectations: Proceeds with the snapshot instead of refusing it as a Data Guard deployment
Reports the source as a Data Guard primary (deploymentType dataguard-primary) rather than plain standalone
Still creates a crash-consistent consistency-group snapshot with no RMAN quiescing
Does not attempt to change, defer, or disable redo transport on the primary

evals.name: clone-dataguard-primary-does-not-join-config
evals.prompt: Clone Oracle SID prod1 on i-0ccccccccccccccc (us-west-2) onto i-0ddddddddddddddd. New SID DGCLONE, port 1522, retention 'dg-clone'. (Source is a Data Guard primary with one physical standby.)
expectations: Proceeds with the clone rather than refusing the Data Guard primary source
Generates a fresh pfile for DGCLONE with no log_archive_dest to the standby, no log_archive_config/DG_CONFIG, no fal_server, and no dg_broker_start
Sets db_unique_name to the clone's own name so the clone cannot be mistaken for a Data Guard member
Keeps db_name as the source's db_name (it is baked into the cloned controlfile)
Does not modify the production primary's or standby's Data Guard configuration

evals.name: database-pdb-on-dataguard-primary-refused
evals.prompt: Create a PDB called SALES in CDB prod1 on i-0ccccccccccccccc, us-west-2, admin user pdbadmin. (Topology discovery reports database_role=PRIMARY with one standby destination.)
expectations: Refuses to create the PDB because the CDB is a Data Guard primary
Explains that CREATE PLUGGABLE DATABASE propagates to the standby, which must materialize the new datafiles
Does not run the CREATE PLUGGABLE DATABASE DDL
Does not conflate this with the snapshot/clone case, which does allow a Data Guard primary

evals.name: snapshot-need-input-filesystem-id
evals.prompt: Snapshot Oracle SID orcl on unregistered host i-0ddddddddddddddd, eu-west-1, retention 'ip-mount-test'. (The NFS mount is by raw IP, so filesystemId cannot be auto-derived.)
expectations: Detects the need_input=filesystemId response from mapped-volume discovery
Asks the operator for the FSx filesystemId instead of guessing it from the IP
Re-runs mapped-volume discovery once filesystemId is supplied
Does not proceed to any mutating call before filesystemId is resolved

evals.name: snapshot-iscsi-protocol
evals.prompt: Take a crash-consistent snapshot of Oracle SID orcl2 on host i-0eeeeeeeeeeeeeeee, us-east-1, retention 'iscsi-snap'. (Storage is iSCSI-attached LUNs, not NFS.)
expectations: Resolves mapped ONTAP LUNs via the iSCSI branch of mapped-ontap-volumes discovery
Confirms the volume/LUN list with the operator before any mutation
Creates a crash-consistent group snapshot covering the resolved LUNs
Does not require ASM- or NFS-specific steps for an iSCSI-only source

evals.name: database-happy-path-pdb-creation
evals.prompt: Create a pluggable database called REPORTING in the CDB with SID orclcdb on host i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890, us-east-1. Admin user pdbadmin, password Str0ngP@ss1.
expectations: Runs topology discovery and confirms isCDB=true and openMode=READ WRITE before any DDL
Does not call aws ssm send-command from the operator machine
Normalizes/validates pdbName and pdbAdminUser against Oracle identifier rules (folds both to uppercase, never the password)
Preflights that REPORTING does not already exist in V$PDBS
Presents a confirmation naming the pdbName and admin user (never the password) before creating it
Waits for an explicit affirmative before running CREATE PLUGGABLE DATABASE
Never echoes, logs, or writes the PDB admin password to a result file
Verifies the PDB exists and is OPEN READ WRITE via a V$PDBS query, not just DDL exit code
Reports verified=true

evals.name: database-noncdb-target-refused
evals.prompt: Create a pluggable database called SALES on Oracle SID orclsa on host i-0fedcba987654321, us-west-2, admin user salesadmin, password Test1234!. (Topology discovery reports isCDB=false.)
expectations: Runs topology discovery before attempting any PDB creation
Refuses to proceed once isCDB is false
Explains that PDB creation requires an existing CDB and that provisioning a brand-new non-CDB instance is out of scope

evals.name: database-duplicate-pdb-refused
evals.prompt: Create pluggable database BILLING in CDB orclcdb2 on host i-0aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa, us-east-1, admin user billadmin, password Pass1234!. (Preflight shows BILLING already exists in V$PDBS.)
expectations: Detects that BILLING already exists via the V$PDBS preflight check
Refuses to run CREATE PLUGGABLE DATABASE and does not drop/recreate the existing PDB
Explains to the user that the PDB already exists

evals.name: database-invalid-identifier-rejected
evals.prompt: Create a pluggable database called 'My PDB!' in CDB orclcdb on host i-0bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb, us-east-2, admin user x, password y.
expectations: Rejects the PDB name for failing the Oracle identifier pattern instead of quoting or sanitizing it
Does not attempt CREATE PLUGGABLE DATABASE with the invalid name
Asks the user for a valid identifier

evals.name: database-rac-cdb-refused
evals.prompt: Create pluggable database ANALYTICS in CDB racdb1 on host i-0ccccccccccccccc, us-east-1, admin user aadmin, password Pass1234!. (Topology discovery reports cluster_database=TRUE.)
expectations: Runs topology discovery before attempting any PDB creation
Refuses to proceed once RAC is detected
States that only single-instance CDBs are supported

evals.name: database-no-premature-confirmation-treated-as-yes
evals.prompt: Please create a PDB called INVENTORY on our Oracle CDB.
expectations: Asks for the missing source identity (registered databaseHostId or unregistered sourceInstanceId), region, oracleSid, and PDB admin credentials before doing anything
Does not run CREATE PLUGGABLE DATABASE in the same turn as the initial request
Only proceeds to the confirmation step once all required inputs are known

evals.name: clone-happy-path-nfs-full-clone
evals.prompt: Clone our Oracle instance SID orcl on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 (us-east-1) onto target host i-0fedcba987654321. New SID CLONE1, listener port 1522, retention label 'qa-test'. Same Oracle version on both hosts, target has no active CLONE1 SID and port 1522 is free. Storage is NFS.
expectations: Resolves mapped ONTAP volumes on the source via run-script before any mutation
Invokes the wlmdb POST .../oracle/.../run-script endpoint rather than aws ssm send-command
Runs topology discovery on both source and target before any mutation
Presents three distinct confirmations: new snapshot, FlexClone volumes, and attach+start+resetlogs — not folded into one
Creates a fresh consistency-group snapshot rather than reusing an old one
Creates FlexClone volumes for all 4 file types from member snapshots of the SAME group snapshot
Mounts the cloned NFS volumes on the target at new mount points
Bootstraps a pfile (control_files at the new mount paths, db_name from the source) and an /etc/oratab entry for CLONE1 before starting the instance
Fixes up controlfile paths with the database MOUNTED, between STARTUP MOUNT and OPEN RESETLOGS
Uses STARTUP MOUNT followed by ALTER DATABASE OPEN RESETLOGS — never any pg_resetwal-style shortcut
Verifies V$DATABASE.OPEN_MODE = READ WRITE and a catalog query before reporting success
Reports clonedVolumes, cloneSid=CLONE1, listenerPort=1522, and verified=true

evals.name: clone-version-mismatch-refused
evals.prompt: Clone Oracle host i-0aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa onto i-0bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb, us-east-1, new SID MISMATCH, port 1523, retention 'test'. (Source is Oracle 19c, target already has Oracle 21c installed.)
expectations: Runs topology discovery on both hosts
Detects the Oracle version mismatch (19c vs 21c)
Refuses to proceed with any snapshot/FlexClone/attach step
Explains the version mismatch to the user instead of attempting a cross-version clone

evals.name: clone-active-target-sid-conflict-refused
evals.prompt: Clone Oracle i-0ccccccccccccccc onto i-0ddddddddddddddd, us-west-2, new SID BUSY1, port 1522, retention 'x'. (Target's /etc/oratab already has an entry for BUSY1 with an active instance.)
expectations: Detects that the target already has an active ORACLE_SID matching the requested cloneSid
Refuses to mount clone volumes over the active instance
Does not stop the target's existing Oracle instance to force the clone

evals.name: clone-port-conflict-refused
evals.prompt: Clone Oracle i-0eeeeeeeeeeeeeeee onto i-0fffffffffffffff, eu-west-1, new SID PORTCLASH, port 1521, retention 'x'. (Port 1521 is already in use on the target by another listener.)
expectations: Checks whether the requested listener port is already listening on the target before proceeding
Refuses to proceed or asks for a different port when 1521 is already in use
Does not start the clone's listener on a conflicting port

evals.name: clone-rac-source-refused
evals.prompt: Clone our Oracle instance i-0111111111111111 onto i-0222222222222222, us-east-2, new SID RACCLONE, port 1522, retention 'x'. (Source topology reports cluster_database=TRUE.)
expectations: Runs topology discovery on the source before any mutation
Refuses to clone once RAC is detected
States that only single-instance sources are supported

evals.name: clone-single-confirmation-not-sufficient
evals.prompt: Yes, go ahead and clone Oracle instance i-0333333333333333 onto i-0444444444444444, us-east-1, new SID ONESHOT, port 1522, retention 'x'.
expectations: Does not treat the user's single upfront 'yes, go ahead' as satisfying all three separate confirmation gates
Still presents and waits for confirmation before the snapshot, before the FlexClone creation, and before attach+start+resetlogs individually
Does not skip topology discovery or verification steps because the user said yes upfront

evals.name: clone-resetlogs-verification-failure-stops-and-reports
evals.prompt: Clone Oracle i-0555555555555555 onto i-0666666666666666, us-east-1, new SID FLAKY, port 1522, retention 'x'. (After OPEN RESETLOGS, V$DATABASE.OPEN_MODE unexpectedly still reports MOUNTED.)
expectations: Detects that OPEN_MODE did not return READ WRITE as expected
Does not report the clone as successful in this unverified state
Does not attempt any hand-edited recovery shortcut instead of standard Oracle recovery
Reports the created consistency group, snapshot, and FlexClone volumes so an operator can investigate/clean up

evals.name: clone-asm-diskgroup-rename
evals.prompt: Clone Oracle ASM-managed instance i-0777777777777777 onto i-0888888888888888, us-east-1, new SID ASMCLONE, port 1522, retention 'asm-test'. (Source uses ASM diskgroup +DATA.)
expectations: Detects ASM as the storage protocol via mapped-ontap-volumes discovery

Maps the cloned LUNs to the target host first (new target-specific igroup + lun-map + iscsiadm login), because ASM disks on FSx for ONTAP are LUNs and the target sees no clone disks until they are mapped
Does not treat PROTOCOL=ASM as 'not iSCSI' and skip the LUN mapping, which would leave renamedg/asmcmd with no visible disks
Scans for the newly mapped disks at the ASM layer (oracleasm scandisks or asmcmd afd_scan) before renaming
Renames the cloned diskgroup (e.g. via renamedg) before mounting it, rather than reusing the source's +DATA name
Mounts the renamed diskgroup via asmcmd before starting the clone instance
Does not mount the clone under a diskgroup name that collides with the source

evals.name: clone-registered-source-unregistered-target
evals.prompt: Clone our registered Oracle host oracle-host-abc123 (instance oracle-inst-xyz, SID orcl, us-east-1) onto unregistered target i-0fedcba987654321. New SID QACLONE, port 1522, retention 'qa-test'.
expectations: Uses databaseHostId/databaseInstanceId for the registered source on run-script
Uses raw instanceId (ec2InstanceId) for the unregistered clone target
Does not invent an EC2 id for the registered source

evals.name: snapshot-no-ssm-permission-falls-back-to-operator-send-command
evals.prompt: Take a snapshot of Oracle SID orcl on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890, us-east-1, retention 'qa'. (The wlmdb run-script call returns HTTP 403 AccessDeniedException for ssm:SendCommand.)
expectations: Recognizes the 403/AccessDeniedException as a permissions failure rather than a generic hard stop
Does not run aws ssm send-command itself — composes the command for the operator to run

Builds the equivalent command from the same allowlisted file run-script would have loaded (server/resources/oracle/scripts/admin/<script>), wrapped in the python heredoc for a .py scriptId, so the script text matches what run-script would have executed
Reproduces the args as export lines, since send-command does not inject them
Still requires an explicit later-turn confirmation before handing over the mutating snapshot command
Validates the envelope the operator pastes back instead of trusting their word that it worked

evals.name: target-not-connected-has-no-fallback
evals.prompt: Take a snapshot of Oracle SID orcl on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890, us-east-1, retention 'qa'. (The wlmdb run-script call fails with TargetNotConnected.)
expectations: Reports the failure and stops
Does not offer the aws ssm send-command fallback, since the instance is not SSM-managed and send-command would fail the same way
Explains that the SSM agent / instance profile has to be fixed first
Does not attempt any ONTAP mutation

evals.name: clone-missing-sid-on-multi-instance-host-asks
evals.prompt: Clone our Oracle host oracle-host-multi01 (us-east-1) onto i-0fedcba987654321. New SID QACLONE, port 1522, retention 'qa-test'. (The host runs two Oracle instances, ORCL and FINPROD.)
expectations: Asks which instance to clone instead of picking ORCL, FINPROD, or a default
Does not run any mutating step (snapshot, FlexClone, attach) before the SID is supplied
Explains that a clone copies one instance, not every instance on the host
Does not treat the host identity alone as a complete source
